requirement:
Profiles already collected for a current attempt remain available for
diagnosis when test execution or coverage collection fails. They remain
subject to later replacement under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current`.
rationale:
Obligations from `requirements.test-coverage.failures.profiles`: (a) profiles already collected for a current attempt stay available when test execution fails; (b) they stay available when coverage collection fails; (c) they remain subject to later replacement under `requirements.test-coverage.storage.current`.

(a) Test execution failure: `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_parallel_processes_retries_child_profiles_and_filtered_reruns]` runs `-E test(retries) --retries 0`. The run fails, and the run outcome and attempt outcome are both "failed". It then calls `assert_profiles_present` on the failed attempt. That helper requires non-empty `profraw` files on disk for every recorded profile. The test also asserts that the earlier run's other attempts are still present. The unit test `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[recovery_removes_orphans_and_cache_but_preserves_current_diagnostic_profiles]` marks an attempt "failed", runs cleanup, and asserts that the attempt's `1.profraw` and its failed outcome survive. It also asserts that orphans and the cache are removed.

(b) Coverage collection failure: `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[passing_tests_with_missing_or_corrupt_profiles_fail_collection_and_retain_partial_reports]` has tests that pass but whose profiles are missing or corrupt. It asserts that the command fails with the "partial profiles and reports have been retained" message. It asserts that the run outcome is "failed" and that the good and corrupt attempts still have their profile files on disk. The corrupt attempt has a diagnostic and empty lines, and the missing attempt has a diagnostic. `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[cleanup_failure_is_reported_and_next_collection_removes_orphans]` covers a cleanup failure during collection. It asserts that the previous runs and attempts are unchanged after the failure.

(c) Later replacement: in `real_parallel_processes_retries_child_profiles_and_filtered_reruns`, a later successful `test(retries) --retries 1` run is asserted to remove the failed run directory with its retained profiles (`!failed_run.exists()`). That shows the retained profiles can still be replaced.

The assertions check file existence and size, not only metadata. The tests exercise both failure modes the text names and the replacement boundary, so I found no adequacy gap.

An entry represents either a test awaiting execution or its current attempt.
